name: World War II
hook: Churchill, the Bulge, the code talkers — the handful of WWII answers Jeopardy returns to endlessly.

facts.label: September 2, 1945
facts.statement: The war ended on September 2, 1945, when Japan signed the surrender aboard the USS Missouri; New Zealand's Air Marshal Isitt put down the final signature.

facts.label: the Battle of the Bulge
facts.statement: Hitler's Ardennes Counteroffensive of December 1944 became the Battle of the Bulge — an Allied victory won in snow and freezing cold.

facts.label: Winston Churchill
facts.statement: Churchill led Britain as prime minister and wrote The Second World War; its first volume, The Gathering Storm, was later adapted for television.

facts.label: the Navajo code talkers
facts.statement: Navajo code talkers sent unbreakable messages in their own language, as depicted in Windtalkers; Arizona now marks August 14 in their honor.

facts.label: Anne Frank
facts.statement: Anne Frank and her sister Margot hid in a secret annex in Amsterdam; Miep Gies, who helped hide them, lived to 100.

facts.label: Tokyo Rose
facts.statement: Iva Toguri D'Aquino was convicted of treason as "Tokyo Rose" and pardoned by President Ford in 1977.

facts.label: Rosie the Riveter
facts.statement: Rosie the Riveter was created in a 1943 song — "That little frail can do more than a male can do" — and became the icon of women war workers.
